First, recall the following identity:

$$
\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}
$$

Then, we use the above identity and rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {sech}^{4}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{cosh}^{4}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.$ Then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and compute it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cosh}^{4}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3{u}^{3}}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3{cosh}^{3}⁡x}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{sech}^{3}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
